([[Henderson, Nevada]]) | college = [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] (2016–2020) | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2020) * Second-team All-SEC (2019) * [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-American of the Year]] (2020) * 2x First-team [[Academic All-American]] ([[2019 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2019]], [[2020 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2020]]) * Second-team Academic All-American ([[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2018]]) }} '''Skylar Mays''' (born September 5, 1997) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mays grew up in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] and attended the [[Louisiana State University Laboratory School]], where he began playing on the varsity basketball team when he in eighth grade. He first began to dunk the basketball as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=How LSU guard Skylar Mays turned a tragedy into fuel for his dreams of being selected in the 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30299175/how-lsu-guard-skylar-mays-turned-tragedy-fuel-dreams-being-selected-2020-nba-draft |accessdate=November 14, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 14, 2020}} He was named first-team All-State in his sophomore and junior seasons as he helped lead the Cubs to back to back state championships. As a junior, he averaged 9.1 points, 8.1 assists and 3.2 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_213331ba-c915-5dd6-9933-bb89781f2ec2.html|title=LSU point guard spot taking shape with Skylar Mays, Jalyn Patterson|first=Andrew|last=Lopez|website=[[NOLA.com]]|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] before his senior year and averaged 10.9 points, 5.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 2.7 steals in his only season with the Pilots.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/2019/02/22/skylar-mays-lsu-basketball-tigers-louisiana-state-point-guard/2935059002/|title=Skylar Mays: 4 facts about the LSU men's basketball point guard|work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]]|date=February 22, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Rated a three-star recruit, Mays committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[LSU Tigers basketball|Louisiana State]] during his sophomore year before re-opening his recruitment to other schools shortly before he transferred to Findlay. Mays eventually re-committed to LSU after considering offers from [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels|UNLV]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_a12aefb9-578d-5910-ab7c-9b0ff4c14a06.html|title=Former U-High basketball star Skylar Mays signs with LSU|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=November 18, 2015|access-date=December 4, 2019}} ==College career== Mays became the Tigers' starting point guard during his freshman year, averaging 8.3 points, 2.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals over 31 games (25 starts).{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/basketball/hc-greater-hartford-pro-am-0730-20170729-story.html|title=Tremont Waters' Game Draws Praise In Pro-Am|first=William|last=Paxton|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=July 29, 2017|access-date=December 3, 2019}} As a sophomore, Mays averaged 11.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists as well as 1.6 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_086cdc88-4a96-11e9-859d-6bc0e8debded.html|title=Basketball and books: How LSU guard Skylar Mays, an Academic All-American, is making it all work|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=The Advocate|date=May 19, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} He averaged 13.4 points, 3.3 rebounds 2.1 assists and 1.9 steals per game as a junior and was named second team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and the conference's scholar-athlete of the year.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_3718fc62-7cdf-11e9-9ffc-035ede760dd2.html|title=LSU's Skylar Mays says he's not yet ready to make a decision on his basketball future|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=The Advocate|date=May 22, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_40ebb817-49d7-5e32-a856-c665bf23cdee.html|title=LSU basketball trio racks up All-SEC coaches awards|first=Amie|last=Just|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays scored his 1,000th career point on February 26, 2019 against [[2018–19 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lsureveille.com/daily/skylar-mays-becomes-st-player-in-lsu-history-to-reach/article_106446f0-3a20-11e9-b517-17a570d95b1e.html|title=Skylar Mays becomes 41st player in LSU history to reach 1000 points|first=Brandon|last=Adam|work=[[The Daily Reveille]]|date=February 26, 2019|access-date=February 9, 2020}} After the season, Mays declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but ultimately opted to return to LSU.{{cite news |last1=Just |first1=Arnie |title=LSU’s Skylar Mays, Marlon Taylor withdraw from NBA Draft |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_dfbaad19-09a5-5716-a6be-46b4897d2a68.html |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |work=[[The Times Picayune]] |date=May 28, 2019}} Mays was named preseason first team All-SEC and to the watchlists for the [[Jerry West Award|Jerry West]] and the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Player of the Year]] awards.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/Javonte-Smart-Skylar-Mays-All-SEC-LSU-basketball-team-2019-138051017/|title=Skylar Mays, Javonte Smart land on All-SEC preseason teams|first=Billy|last=Embody|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} He was also named the 45th-best collegiate basketball player going into the 2019–20 season by [[CBS Sports]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-the-top-100-and-1-best-players-in-college-basketball-entering-the-2019-20-season/|title=Ranking the Top 100 And 1 best players in college basketball entering the 2019-20 season|first1=Kyle|last1=Boone|first2=Matt|last2=Norlander|first3=Gary|last3=Parrish|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 24, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays scored a career-high 30 points on November 22, 2019 in an 80–78 loss to [[2019–20 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_798451b2-0d8c-11ea-b769-0398a6ec75c8.html|title=LSU basketball lets 19-point lead slip away in brutal Utah State loss|work=The Advocate|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=January 30, 2020}} Mays tied his career high with 30 points along with eight assists and seven rebounds on February 8, 2020 in a 91–90 overtime loss to [[2019–20 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wafb.com/2020/02/08/game-updates-no-lsu-vs-no-auburn/|title=Mays scores career-high 30 in No. 18 LSU OT loss to No. 10 Auburn|website=[[WAFB|WAFB.com]]|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 9, 2020}} At the end of the regular season he was again named a first team Academic All-American and was selected as the [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-American of the Year]] as well as First Team All-SEC and was named the scholar-athlete of the year for a second straight season.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_668ec6f0-6223-11ea-8045-9748bcdf27f5.html|title=LSU's Skylar Mays is chosen Academic All-America of the Year by CoSIDA organization|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}}{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} Mays averaged 16.7 points and 5.0 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Crawford |first1=Kirkland |title=The 2020 NCAA tournament that could have been: South region friend and LSU teammate, Wayde Sims, was killed by a gunshot wound to the head and neck on September 28, 2018. Mays served as the pallbearer at the funeral.{{cite news |last1=Norlander |first1=Matt |title=Forever 44: How a teammate's murder has brought LSU together and fueled the Tigers' inspired season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/forever-44-how-a-teammates-murder-has-brought-lsu-together-and-fueled-the-tigers-inspired-season/ |accessdate=December 3, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 23, 2019}} He gave an 11-minute speech in Sims's honor at an on-campus vigil outside the [[Pete Maravich Assembly Center]] in front of a crowd of hundreds. Mays wore customized Nike tennis shoes during the 2019 SEC Tournament in honor of Sims.{{cite news |title=LSU guard Skylar Mays honors former teammate Wayde Sims during game against Vanderbilt |url=https://www.wbrz.com/news/lsu-guard-skylar-mays-honors-former-teammate-wayde-sims-during-game-against-vanderbilt/ |accessdate=December 4, 2019 |work=WBRZ |date=March 10, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://lsusports.net/sports/mens-basketball/roster/skylar-mays/5492 LSU Tigers bio] {{Men's Basketball Academic All-America of the Year}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Mays, Skylar}} [[Category:1997 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Louisiana]] [[Category:Findlay Prep alumni]] [[Category:Louisiana State University Laboratory School alumni]] [[Category:LSU Tigers basketball players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Baton Rouge, Louisiana]]
